name: Routeburn Track
region: Mount Aspiring and Fiordland national parks
why: Up the Route Burn to the tops, over Harris Saddle and along the Hollyford Face with the Darran Mountains across the valley.
book: Great Walk: Routeburn Flats, Routeburn Falls and Lake Mackenzie huts and campsites must be booked for 1 Nov-30 Apr. The ends are 325 km apart by road: book transport at both ends (Routeburn Shelter is 25 km from Glenorchy, The Divide 85 km from Te Anau).
water: Tap water at huts and campsites, untreated: boil it. Streams on the way.
dangers: The Harris Saddle and Hollyford Face sections are exposed to wind, rain and snow at any time of year.
Avalanche risk can last into December; DOC may close sections.
Rockfall zones: do not stop where signs say so.
turnaround: If the weather on the tops is bad at Routeburn Falls Hut or Lake Mackenzie Hut, wait or go back down rather than cross Harris Saddle.

points.name: Routeburn Shelter
points.note: Road end 25 km from Glenorchy. The track follows the Route Burn through beech forest.

points.name: Routeburn Falls Hut
points.note: First night, at the bushline beside the Routeburn Falls, about 10 km in.

points.name: Harris Saddle
points.note: Tarahaka Whakatipu, 1,255 m, above Lake Harris. Day shelter with toilets; Conical Hill is a steep 1 h 30 min side trip.

points.name: Lake Mackenzie Hut
points.note: Second night beside Lake Mackenzie, after the traverse of the Hollyford Face.

points.name: The Divide
points.note: Past Earland Falls and Lake Howden down to the Milford Road at 532 m. Key Summit is a 1-1 h 30 min side trip.
